part.text:
Fixed. The issue was that `bitposCommand` (and by symmetry the missing-key path of BITCOUNT) looked up the key and replied with `0`/`-1` before validating the `start`/`end`/`BIT|BYTE` arguments, so illegal arguments silently returned a value when the key was missing.

Change in `src/bitops.c:960` (`bitposCommand`): moved argument parsing/validation (bit, start, end, unit) ahead of the key lookup, so syntax/integer errors are returned regardless of whether the key exists, and only then do the missing-key early reply and type check. Range/default-end computation and negative-index conversion now happen after the string length is known.

Verified: `unit/bitops` (all FAIL_TO_PASS cases including `BITCOUNT/BITPOS with illegal arguments` and `against non-integer value` for missing and wrong-type keys) and `unit/type/string` pass.
